newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union wants full sick pay for bank sector.
newsitem.headline: German union wants full sick pay for bank sector.

text.p: Germany's DAG white-collar workers' union said on Tuesday it would seek to maintain full payment of sick pay entitlements for its 450,000 members when it meets bank employers for a second round of talks on Wednesday.

DAG's chief negotiator Gerhard Renner said in a statement the potential savings to be made from implementing the controversial sick pay benefit cuts were insignificant because the sector was at the bottom end of the scale on absenteeism.
The negotiations were scheduled to begin at 0900 GMT on Wednesday in Koenigstein near Frankfurt.
The union also said wage increases should reflect the excellent situation in the banking industry and measures to ensure employment would be a top priority at the discussions.

German bank employers last month decided to postpone implementing 20 percent reductions in sick pay benefits, allowed under a new German law passed in late 1996, until a wider agreement for industry workers had been reached.
The decision came after protests were held by some 15,000 bank employees in protest against sick pay cuts by most of the major commercial banks, including Deutsche Bank, the country's largest bank.

The banking sector is the only industry in Germany where employers have acted together to enforce the law, which was part of an austerity package introduced by Bonn to ensure German entry to the single European currency in 1999.

German bank employers say wage contracts in their sector, unlike some in the chemical and engineering industries, do not specify sick pay at 100 percent of salary and that they are free to impose the cuts.
